description: Logomania is a exaggerated, high-influenced fashion style that originated in the 1980s characterized by the repetitive use of luxurious, oversized, or highly visible use of brand logos, monograms, and luxury symbols across clothing, interior design and accessories. Despite its roots being tied to fashion houses in Europe, its current shape was dominated by the aesthetic in the 1980s Harlem, New York whose efforts and luxurious elements were sampled by Dapper Dan to create casual streetwear for the hip-hop movement. During its shift, its practices transformed corporate, clean branding into a bold, repeating style that incorporates sleek, high-visibility status symbols over a subtle and sterile design, originated as a status embodiment of belonging and wealth which has evolved into a cyclical cultural phenomenon/movement, diffusing casual streetwear with luxury and irony.
culturalContext: Logomania was created by Dapper Dan in Harlem, New York during the 1980s.
